sara-support: FYI we just got a customer escalation — all action buttons on a project console are disabled (view-only) and any attempt to edit shows a 403. Customer says this started after an IdP change.

sara-support: Repro steps from customer:
1) Login via SSO (Okta)
2) Open org > project > click Edit project
3) UI shows buttons but clicking Edit returns: 403 modal 'Permission denied'

sara-support: I grabbed a raw API repro they ran with their ephemeral session: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL_TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/abcd123/edit \n  -d '{"name":"test"}'
```
Response body: 
```json
{
  "error": "forbidden",
  "reason": "missing_scope",
  "detail": "required: project.edit, granted: project.view"
}
```

sara-support: Customer says their Okta group->role mapping was recently edited to shorten claim length (to reduce token size). They suspect truncation. Ticket: INC-5120.

jamie-eng: thanks — can you paste the trimmed claim example (sanitized) and the raw id_token payload if available?

sara-support: pasted in DM. Summary: groups claim is a comma-separated list; for this user it ended abruptly ("team-admins,project-ow") which cut off the full name that maps to project.admin role.

jamie-eng: that matches a mapping miss — when SCIM/group names are long we rely on exact match. If mapping key is truncated the role won't be assigned. Quick check: run our auth inspect endpoint with the user's token:
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/inspect | jq .claims.groups
```
If that list is truncated, that's the root cause.

olivia-security: also confirm whether this is an idempotent session (session created pre-trim) vs newly minted token post-trim. Old sessions can retain roles; new tokens will reflect new claims.

jamie-eng: workaround for the customer: we can either force a SCIM resync for the org or create a short-lived role binding for the affected user. Prefer resync so it fixes others.

mike-sre: adding resync command (internal tool):
```bash
# force SCIM/group sync for org acme-corp
./tools/scimctl sync --org acme-corp --force --dry-run
# inspect membership changes then run without --dry-run
```
If customer wants immediate unblock: create a temporary project edit binding via support console CLI:
```bash
./support-cli grant --org acme-corp --project abcd123 --user user@example.com --role project.editor --ttl 1h
```

sara-support: I'll propose the resync + short-lived grant and ask them to sign out/sign back in after resync. Will confirm token inspection results.

olivia-security: long-term we should add a defensive mapping that tolerates truncated claim fragments or prefer group IDs instead of raw names. Filing follow-up: SEC-2340 (claim-tolerance).

idp-bot: Note: scheduled SCIM batch for acme-corp at 2026-03-18T03:00Z (can be triggered manually).

mike-sre: assigning to jamie-eng for the codefix and olivia-security for policy. tag: @jamie-eng @olivia-security :page_with_curl:

sara-support: thanks all — I'll update the customer and attach these repro steps + the recommended mitigation. :thumbsup:
